subject: social-work
intro: Social work leads to the paid work of standing beside people when systems fail them — casework in schools and hospitals, crisis response, community programmes and the policy advocacy that reshapes them.

roles.title: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
roles.what: Support children and families through hard patches: investigate abuse and neglect concerns, arrange foster care and adoptions, link parents to benefits and services, and help students and families keep school life on track.
roles.where: Unit 5's case management and crisis intervention, unit 4's biopsychosocial assessment, and the child-development strand of unit 2 are the exact tools this casework runs on.

roles.title: Healthcare Social Workers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree; MSW for clinical roles
roles.what: Help patients live with illness and navigate the health system: plan discharges, arrange home care and equipment, counsel families facing terminal diagnosis, and connect people to financial help and community services.
roles.where: The biopsychosocial assessment model from unit 4, human-behaviour-across-the-life-course content from unit 2, and the field-education practicum of unit 9 mirror this role's hospital and discharge work.

roles.title: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
roles.what: Treat people living with mental illness and addiction: run therapy and relapse-prevention groups, build recovery and treatment plans, respond in crises, and help clients hold onto housing, work and relationships while they recover.
roles.where: Unit 5's crisis intervention and family systems work, plus the engagement skills and working-alliance training in unit 4, are the clinical core this licence builds on.

roles.title: Social and Human Service Assistants
roles.what: Work under social workers and psychologists: help clients fill in paperwork for benefits, arrange transport to appointments, check in on people in supported housing, and record how clients are progressing in case files.
roles.where: The generalist-practice frame of unit 1, engagement skills from unit 4 and the documentation habits of the field-education unit describe this entry-level role almost exactly.

roles.title: Social and Community Service Managers
roles.what: Run the programmes behind the services: write funding proposals, hire and supervise staff and volunteers, manage budgets, measure whether a programme actually works, and speak for the community it serves.
roles.where: Unit 6's community organising and macro-level change, unit 8's programme evaluation, and unit 7's policy analysis are precisely the management craft this job is paid for.
